questions.question: Which part of Human ear collects sound from its surrounding?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Option **1** i.e **__Pinna__**.

 
 

 __**Pinna**__
 
 
 
• The **pinna** is the **only visible part of the ear** with its **special helical shape**.
 
• It acts as a kind of funnel that assists in **directing the sound further into the ear**.
 
• This is the **outside part of the ear**, collects sound from the environment or surroundings.
 
 
 
 

 Cochlea
 
 
 
• The **cochlea** is a portion of the **inner ear**.
 
• It looks like a **snail shell**.
 
• The function of the cochlea is to **transform the vibrations of the cochlear liquids** and associated structures into a **neural signal**.
 
 
 
 

 Anvil
 
 
 
• In the **middle ear**, there are three tiny bones (ossicles) - the hammer (malleus), anvil (incus) and stirrup (stapes).
 
• Also called the incus, a tiny bone **that passes vibrations from the hammer to the stirrup**.
 
 
 
 

 Hammer
 
 
 
• It is also called the **Malleus**.
 
• It is a tiny bone that passes vibrations from the eardrum to the anvil.

questions.question: Mountain Building on the surface of the earth is a result of which type of Forces?
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 1__ i.e __Endogenic Forces__.**

__
 
• **Endogenic forces__: **

 __
 
• These are **internal forces** that originate from **within the surface of the earth**. ​​
 
• These internal forces lead to **vertical and horizontal movements** and result in subsidence, land upliftment, volcanism, faulting, folding, earthquakes, etc.
 
• **Mountain Building** on the surface of the earth is a result of the **Endogenic Force**__.
 
 
 
• Exogenic forces:
 
 
• These are external forces, that occur on or above the earth's surface.
 
• Weathering, mass wasting, erosion, and deposition are the main exogenic processes.
 
 
 
• Gravitational Force
 
 
• The gravitational force is a force that attracts any two objects with mass.
 
• Examples include the force that holds the gases in the sun and the force that causes a ball you throw in the air to come down again.
 
• This is the weakest force among all the fundamental forces.
 
 
 
• Magnetic Force:
 
 
• It is an attractive force between two moving charges.
 
• Examples of magnetic force are a compass, a motor, train tracks, etc.

questions.question: President of INTERPOL elected in November 2018 belongs to which Country?
questions.solution:
The **Correct Answer** is Option **1** i.e **__South Korea__**.

 
• The **International Criminal Police Organisation (INTERPOL)** is an **international organization** that facilitates worldwide police cooperation and crime control.

• It was **founded in 1923** as the **International Criminal Police Commission (ICPC)**.
 
• In November 2018, INTERPOL's General Assembly elected Kim to fill the remainder of Meng's term.

• Interpol issues notice to communicate information about crimes, criminals to their counterparts around the world.
 
• There are **eight types of notices**, seven of which are color-coded by their function: **Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Black, Orange, and Purple**.
 
• The most well-known notice is the Red Notice which is the "**closest instrument to an international arrest warrant in use today**".
 
• An **eighth Special Notice** is issued at the request of the **United Nations Security Council**.

questions.question: In which coastal town did Mahatma Gandhi break 'Salt law'?
questions.solution:
The **Correct Answer** is Option 3 i.e **__Dandi__**.

 
• **Dandi March or Salt Satyagraha** was a non-violent means of protest led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Salt Satyagraha March started on 12th March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram and reached Dandi after 24 days on 6th April 1930.
 
• The movement began with Gandhi’s march from Sabarmati to the coastal town of Dandi in Gujarat.
 
• On **6th April**, Gandhi reached Dandi where **he broke the Salt Law**.
 
• During colonial rule, salt production and distribution in India used to be controlled by the British government.
 
• Through a series of legislation, Indians were prohibited from producing and selling salt independently, instead, the general Indian population was required to buy heavily taxed imported salt.
 
• Gandhi through his Dandi March protested against the regressive policies of the British Government.
 
• The **Ahmedabad Mill-Hand's strike** happened during **February-March 1918**.
 
• Gandhi used the Satyagraha and hunger strike for the first time in an industrial dispute between the owners and workers of a cotton mill in Ahmedabad.
 
• **INC split** took place in Surat in 1907 under **Rash Bihari Ghosh**.

questions.question: Bats search out prey and fly in dark night by emitting and detecting reflections of which type of Sound Waves?
questions.solution:
**__CONCEPT__**:

__
 
• Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves and frequency can be defined as the number of wave cycle happening in one sec.
 
• The types of sound waves whose frequencies is higher than the upper audible limit of human hearing is called an Ultrasound/Ultrasonic wave.
 
• Ultrasonic waves or Ultrasound waves: The sound frequency above 20,000Hz is known as ultrasonic waves. Humans cannot detect it too.
 
• Examples: Bat produce Ultrasonic waves.
 
• A Subsonic wave is a wave that is traveling slower than the speed of sound.
 
• Hypersonic wave is one that greatly exceeds the speed of sound, often starting at speeds of Mach 5 and above.

**EXPLANATION__:**.

 
• When the ultrasonic wave produced by the bats strike with the obstacle/food or prey of the bats then it come back at bats.
 
• Then bats run along in the direction of that obstacle/prey and catches the food. 
 
• Thus **bats can detect and produce the ultrasonic wave in due to which it can catch the prey in dark night **also. So option 1 is correct.

questions.question: What is the main mineral constituent of Continental mass?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Option **4** i.e **__Silica and Alumina__**.

It is also called as **SiAl**. **(Si - Silica, Al - Alumina)**.

 
• Structure of the earth is fundamentally divided into three layers: They are
 
 
• Crust
 
• Mantle
 
• Core
 
 
 
• **Crust**: It is the outermost solid part of the earth's surface, brittle in nature.
 
 
• The crust is **only about 8 kilometers thick** under the **oceans (oceanic crust)** and about **32 kilometers thick under the continents (continental crust)**.
 
• Major constituent elements of crust are **Silica (Si) and Aluminium (Al)** and thus, it is often termed as **SIAL**.
 
 
 
• **Mantle**: The layer beyond the earth's crust is called the mantle.
 
 
• The major constituent elements of the mantle are **Silicon and Magnesium** and hence it is also termed as **SIMA**.
 
 
 
• **Core**: It is the innermost layer of the earth.
 
 
• Earth’s Core is thought to be composed mainly of an **iron and nickel** alloy and hence it is also termed as **NIFE**.

questions.question: Which act of the Parliament set targets for the government to reduce fiscal deficits in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__FRBM Act.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__FRBM Act__:

The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003** is an Indian law aimed at promoting fiscal prudence and macroeconomic stability.

**Key features of the FRBM Act:**

__
 
• **Fiscal deficit targets**: The Act sets specific targets for the fiscal deficit, which are reviewed periodically.
 
• **Debt and liabilities ceilings**: The Act also sets limits on the government's debt and liabilities as a percentage of GDP.
 
• **Escape clause**: The Act includes an escape clause that allows the government to deviate from the fiscal deficit target in exceptional circumstances, such as during natural disasters or national emergencies.
 
• **Independent fiscal council:** The Act provides for the establishment of an independent fiscal council to monitor the government's compliance with the Act's provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA):** 

 
• It was introduced in the year **1973**.
 
• The act was introduced to **regulate inflow and outflow** of foreign currency, foreign payments, securities and purchase of fixed assets by the foreigners.

**FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act)**

 
• It was introduced in the year **1999** to **replace an earlier act FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act)**.
 
• It was formulated to promote the orderly development and maintenance of foreign exchange market in India.

**RBI Act**:

 
• It was established in **1935** under the **RBI Act 1934**.
 
• RBI was nationalized on **1 January 1949**.
 
• Present RBI Governor: **Shaktikanta Das**

**POSCO Act**:

 
• It was enacted in **2012** to provide a legal framework for the protection of children from sexual offenses.
 
• The **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act,** **2012 **came into force with effect on** 14 November 2012.** 
 
• The Act defines a **child as any person below 18 years of age** and defines different forms of sexual abuse including penetrative and non-penetrative assault as well as sexual harassment and pornography.

questions.question: Which of the following landforms does NOT depict the youthful Stage of rivers?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Option** 3 **i.e** __Delta__.**

There are **three stages** of the river:

 
• **Youthful stage**

 
 
• A river with a steep gradient that has very few tributaries and flows quickly.
 
• Its channels erode deeper rather than wider.
 
• Its velocity is fast and strong
 
• **Rapids **may be present due to the water velocity and the presence of boulders in the channel
 
• waterfalls are also a feature of the young river.
 
• Shallow V-shaped valleys are present.
 
 
 
• **Mature stage:**
 
 
• The channel of Mature river is **U shaped** but deeper than and not as wide as old river channels.
 
• Rapids are absent so is the **V-shaped channel**.
 
• Deep V-shaped valleys are present.
 
 
 
• **Old stage**
 
 
• When the river reaches the end of its journey, it is called an **old river**.
 
• The end of the river is called the mouth and at the mouth, there is often a **river delta**.
 
 
 
• **Gorge** is a narrow valley with steep rocky walls on both sides and a river usually flowing in between.
